about.heading: Driven
about.text: I come from retail and sales and at some point realized that creating things interests me more than selling them. That is why I am currently completing a one-year full-stack program and spending my evenings working on my own projects. What I enjoy most is digging into a new topic until I truly understand why something works.
about.text_2: Order and structure matter a lot to me, in everyday life as much as in code. I quickly notice when something is not organised properly and find it hard to leave it that way. In development, that is an advantage: clear names, a well-structured codebase and components with one clear purpose. It means I can still find my way around my code weeks later — and so can others on the team.

coderr.name: Coderr
coderr.image_alt: The Coderr homepage with an IT services search and platform statistics
coderr.description: The backend for a digital services marketplace. It manages user profiles, offers, orders and reviews and provides the data through a REST API.
coderr.umsetzung: Built with Python, Django and Django REST Framework. Separate apps handle authentication and profiles, offers, orders, reviews and platform statistics. SQLite stores data locally. The matching frontend is provided by Developer Akademie.
coderr.learnings: The focus is on the relationships between offers, orders and reviews, with serializers, views and permissions organised separately. Registration and login use token authentication; pytest and pytest-django are included for testing.

kanmind.name: KanMind
kanmind.image_alt: The KanMind dashboard with a task overview, status chart and board list
kanmind.description: The backend for a Kanban-style project management tool. Its REST API manages boards, tasks and comments and provides assigned tasks and tasks awaiting review.
kanmind.umsetzung: Built with Python, Django and Django REST Framework. An authentication app handles registration and login, while a Kanban app groups boards, tasks, comments and permissions. Data is stored locally in SQLite. The matching frontend is provided by Developer Akademie.
kanmind.learnings: The API models the relationships between boards, tasks and comments. Other areas of focus include token authentication, access permissions and dedicated endpoints for assigned tasks and reviews.

join.name: Join
join.description: A typical Kanban board for task management. You can create tasks, assign them to people and move them from 'To Do' to 'Done' via drag and drop.
join.learnings: The biggest challenge was actually working with four people on the same codebase. You quickly realize how important clear Git workflows are. Towards the end, I took some time to properly clean up and structure the code.
join.umsetzung: I mainly took care of the summary dashboard. I also built the drag and drop logic for the board and created the required legal pages.
join.image_alt: The Join kanban board with the columns To Do, In Progress and Done

dabubble.name: DABubble
dabubble.description: A sort of Slack clone for teams. You can chat in channels or directly with each other and reply to messages in threads – all in real time, of course.
dabubble.learnings: It got really tricky when I had to make sure that the sidebar, chat area, and open threads always stayed in sync without interfering with each other when new messages arrived.
dabubble.umsetzung: I built the entire chat interface. We used Angular for the frontend and hooked up Supabase as the database, with the chat relying on Supabase's real-time subscriptions. Aside from that, I also built the auth, profiles, and a search feature.
dabubble.image_alt: The DABubble chat interface with channel list, message history and an open thread

el_pollo_loco.name: El Pollo Loco
el_pollo_loco.description: A small jump and run game that I wrote entirely in plain JavaScript. The main character collects coins and salsa bottles to defeat a boss enemy at the end.
el_pollo_loco.learnings: Collision detection definitely gave me the biggest headache. When exactly do you jump on an enemy, and when do you take damage yourself? Encapsulating all of this flawlessly in objects and classes was a great exercise.
el_pollo_loco.umsetzung: Everything was built from scratch in vanilla JavaScript. It features a custom game loop, object hierarchies for the enemies, and some basic state management for the game phases.
el_pollo_loco.image_alt: A gameplay scene from El Pollo Loco with the player character, coin counter and enemies

pokedex.name: Pokedex
pokedex.description: A kind of encyclopedia for Pokémon. The data is pulled live from the PokeAPI. You can scroll through all Pokémon, filter them, and view their exact stats.
pokedex.learnings: Since the API requires an enormous amount of individual requests for certain things, the page was initially very slow. I had to learn how to smartly batch requests and optimize loading times.
pokedex.umsetzung: Mostly asynchronous JavaScript (Fetch) to retrieve the data, combined with search and filter logic for the frontend.
pokedex.image_alt: The Pokedex overview with Pokémon cards and a search field

The data you enter will remain with me until you ask me to delete it, revoke your consent, or the purpose for data storage no longer applies (e.g. after your request has been processed). Mandatory legal provisions – in particular retention periods – remain unaffected.

In addition, an irreversible check value (hash) of your IP address is stored on the server for a maximum of one hour in order to limit the number of requests per sender. After that, the entry is deleted automatically. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest in preventing misuse).
